Bill Zerella, Known for Taking Startups Public, on Why He Joined Stord as CFO

Plus, Anthropic raises $81 billion in biggest IPO ever

By

Good morning, CFOs. There are CFOs who take companies public. And then there are CFOs who do it again and again. Bill Zerella is the latter.

That’s what interested me about Zerella, who recently joined the supply-chain company Stord as CFO. Stord is a venture-backed company that helps merchants compete with bigger retailers by offering them an e-commerce platform attached to physical fulfillment centers. The company has had a big year, raising $250 million in a Series F fundraising round, and completing a sizable acquisition.

Newsletter Sign-up

WSJ | CFO Journal

The Morning Ledger provides daily news and insights on corporate finance from the CFO Journal team.

I asked Zerella whether Stord, by hiring him as CFO, is signaling its ambitions to do a public offering. He said the company is focused on scaling the business—adding more physical infrastructure, and doing so with a path toward profitability.

But Zerella’s track record shepherding companies into the public markets speaks for itself. During his nearly three decades as a CFO, he’s taken three venture-backed companies public: online car auction marketplace ACV Auctions in 2021; personal fitness tracker Fitbit in 2015, before Google acquired it in 2021; and healthcare technology firm Vocera Communications in 2012, before Stryker acquired it in 2022.
